findings.title: AC2 "same values for every shared key" cannot hold for started_at and interrupted
findings.detail: `runner.write_run_record` takes `started_at` from the runner's own `_now_iso()` clock, while the fallback uses the `run.start` event's `ts`. Those are different timestamps, possibly in different formats. `interrupted` also differs. In `run.json` it is `result.interrupted`, which is always False for ClaudeRunner. In `run.end` it is `interrupted or result.interrupted`, the step's view (`queue._record_run`). A test that deletes `run.json` and compares every shared key will fail, or the implementer will have to guess. Either narrow AC2 to a named list of keys and say that `started_at` and `interrupted` are exempt, or state which source wins and how the format is normalised.

findings.title: Which runs are listed is not specified
findings.detail: The spec never says what enumerates the runs: the `runs/` directories, the ledger `run.start`/`run.end` events, or their union. The cases differ. A `run.json` with no ledger events is one. A ledger run whose directory was deleted is another. A run dir with `prompt.md` only is a third, and so is a crash between `run.start` and `run.end` (the `running` case). Without a rule the ordering by `run_id`, the `status: running` rule and the RUN prefix matching are ambiguous. Specify the union keyed by `run_id`, the precedence when both exist, and what a run dir with neither `run.json` nor ledger events does.

findings.title: transient derives from result_tail, which is empty for most runs
findings.detail: `queue._record_run` writes `result_tail` only when `not verdict_ok`, and it truncates it to 400 characters. A timed-out run with a valid verdict, or any failure whose tail was blank, therefore always gets `transient: false`. `events.run_failed` falls back to the text `"timed out"` or `"error"` before calling `_is_transient`, but the spec uses `result_tail or ""`. State this deliberately, or reuse the same fallback so the two views agree. Also note that `result_tail` comes from the ledger even when `source` is `run.json`, so a run with `run.json` and no `run.end` has an empty tail.

findings.title: verdict_status edge cases are undefined
findings.detail: The spec does not say what happens when `verdict` is not a dict, when a dict has none of `status`, `disposition` or `verdict`, or when the value is not a string. It also does not say whether `invalid` takes precedence over the fallback chain when `verdict_ok` is false and a status is present. Add one sentence for each. The colour map (done/pass/blocked/fail/escalate) should be cross-checked against the real persona verdict vocabularies.

findings.title: cost column ignores charged_usd
findings.detail: The `cost` column shows `cost_usd`, which is null when the runner reported no cost. The ledger then charges the pessimistic budget as `charged_usd`. The diagnostic purpose of the idea (429 parks) benefits from seeing what was charged. Either add `charged_usd` (ledger only) or say that `cost_usd` is shown and null renders as `—`.

findings.title: stderr_tail and permission_denials edge handling
findings.detail: Say what happens when `result.json` is empty or unparseable, which is common for failed runs (it is already `[]` by the wording, so confirm that it is tested). Also say whether `stderr_tail` is a list of lines or a joined string in JSON. The pinned shapes elsewhere leave this open.

findings.title: Only one alternative
findings.detail: Consider recording why the new command does not extend `wt campaign log --type run.end` with filters, or why it does not go under `wt campaign show`.
